posts.excerpt: Africa Evidence Week | August 19 – 23, 2024 Event 1 Evaluating Systematic Review Training Programs: Insights, Challenges & Future Directions About the Event Join us for an engaging webinar as we delve into an evaluation of the African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (ACSRM) traini
posts.text: Africa Evidence Week | August 19 – 23, 2024 Event 1 Evaluating Systematic Review Training Programs: Insights, Challenges & Future Directions About the Event Join us for an engaging webinar as we delve into an evaluation of the African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (ACSRM) training programs. Since our inception in 2022, ACSRM has been dedicated to building capacity in evidence synthesis across Low-and Middle-income countries, especially in the African continent. In this session, we will share key insights from our evaluation, highlighting the challenges faced, successes achieved, and future directions for our programs. We will begin with the findings of our systematic review and meta-analysis needs assessment conducted in 2022. We will then present an overview of our evaluation process, including the methodologies and tools used to assess the impact of our training programs. Participants will learn about common challenges encountered in organising and delivering these programs, such as resource constraints, participant engagement, and curriculum customisation. Additionally, we will celebrate our successes, showcasing positive outcomes and participant testimonials that reflect the transformative impact of our training efforts. Looking ahead, we will outline strategic improvements and new initiatives aimed at enhancing our capacity-building activities. This webinar will feature a dynamic panel discussion with experts who will provide their insights on the evaluation findings and share best practices in capacity building. Interactive polls and a Q&A session will offer participants the opportunity to engage actively and share their experiences. This is an opportunity to gain valuable insights and contribute to the conversation on advancing evidence synthesis training in Africa. Event Date and Time Date: August 20, 2024 Time: 1:30 pm – 2:30 pm GMT Event Links https://shorturl.at/0ODZi https://x.com/ACSRMofficial https://systematicreviewsnetwork.org Event 2 Communicating Evidence: Hand-On Workshop on Translation & Dissemination About The Event The African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (ACSRM) invites researchers to participate in a hands-on workshop aimed at enhancing skills in communicating and translating evidence synthesis findings. This interactive session is designed to provide practical strategies for improving the impact of research through effective dissemination. The workshop will commence with an introduction to the principles of knowledge translation, focusing on how to transform complex evidence into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences. Techniques for crafting impactful research summaries and targeting specific groups, such as academics, policymakers, and practitioners, will be covered. Participants will engage in practical exercises, including writing research summaries and developing dissemination plans tailored to different stakeholders. The workshop will also showcase the use of digital tools and platforms, such as social media and blogs, to expand the reach and influence of research findings. The session will feature interactive Q&A and discussions, allowing participants to share their experiences and seek advice on overcoming their own dissemination challenges. By the end of this workshop, attendees will be better prepared to communicate their evidence synthesis findings effectively and maximise their impact. Event Date and Time Date: August 23, 2024 Time: 1:30 pm – 3:30 pm GMT Event Links https://shorturl.at/0ODZi https://x.com/ACSRMofficial https://systematicreviewsnetwork.org

posts.text: Introduction: African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (ACSRM) is a community of practice established to support the production and use of Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (SRM) in LMICs. Leveraging the success of our prior webinars and workshops, we're excited to announce a four-day intensive systematic review workshop at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in Kumasi, Ghana. The workshop will be held from July 1st to 5th, 2024. This workshop is designed to equip participants with the practical skills to conduct systematic reviews. Participants will benefit from expert instruction, build valuable connections with fellow researchers, and earn a certificate upon completion Calling All Postgraduate Research Champions! Are you a dedicated faculty member or student leader passionate about empowering your postgraduate program in evidence-based research methodologies, particularly systematic reviews? Become a Postgraduate School Liaison and Bridge the Gap! We are seeking passionate faculty members or research students at postgraduate schools to join our team as Systematic Review Workshop Liaisons. In this vital role, you will facilitate a successful collaboration between our workshops and relevant departments within your school, such as research methods, public health, or epidemiology. What You Will Do: Raise Awareness: Spread the word about the workshop within your postgraduate program through various channels (e.g., emails, student presentations, faculty meetings). Collaboration Champion: Act as a liaison between your postgraduate program and our organization in our forthcoming systematic review workshop. Benefits for You and Your Program: Increased Engagement: Boost postgraduate student and faculty participation in systematic reviews training opportunities. Branding and Recognition: Your postgraduate program and your name will be featured as a valued partner on our workshop materials and website. Networking Opportunities: Connect with other research enthusiasts across different postgraduate programs. Join the Movement! By becoming a Postgraduate School Liaison, you'll directly contribute to strengthening research capacity within your postgraduate program and the broader academic community. How to Apply: Visit our website for more details about the workshop . Contact us at acsrm.int@gmail.com to express your interest and apply for the Liaison role. Deadline to express interest: May 31, 2024

posts.title: Advancing Systematic Reviews Production and Use: The Evolution of International Systematic Rview Network
posts.excerpt: Written by: Fortune Effiong Systematic reviews of research are increasingly recognized as important for informing decisions across policy sectors and for setting priorities for research. posts.text: Written by: Fortune Effiong Systematic reviews of research are increasingly recognized as important for informing decisions across policy sectors and for setting priorities for research. Over the years, several international organizations have been created to support the production and use of systematic reviews around the world. These International organizations have a shared interest of strengthening systematic review production and use in both HICs and LMICs. Efforts to establish systematic review networks began with the founding of The Cochrane Collaboration in 1993. Cochrane is an international network of researchers and healthcare advocates that supports the production and use of systematic reviews for evidence-based healthcare. The cochrane library contains different types of high-quality evidence to inform healthcare decision making. The Cochrane Collaboration is the largest systematic review network in terms of skilled workforce and established centers. The Cochrane Collaboration has developed review groups and centers in both HICs and LMICS, often hosted by higher education institutions, to foster the production of systematic reviews. Cochrane members and supporters come from more than 190 countries. Similar to Cochrane, The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) in 1996 to support evidence-based health care. The Joanna Briggs Institute Evidence-Based Practice Database provides systematic reviews, practice guidelines, and consumer information to assist evidence-based practice in healthcare. JBI's critical appraisal instruments allow researchers to evaluate the reliability, applicability, and outcomes of published articles. The JBI Collaboration has more than 75 Collaborating entities across 40 countries. The Campbell Collaboration was created in 1999, and they support reviews that are focussed on education, behavioral science, social justice and social welfare. The Campbell Collaboration establishes coordinating groups to facilitate systematic reviews and production in various areas of practice. Campbell Collaboration Coordinating Groups (CGs) include: Ageing GC; Business and Management GCs; Children and Young Persons Wellbeing GC; Climate Solutions GC; Social Welfare GC; Crime and Justice GC; Disability GC; Education GC; International Development GC; Knowledge, Translation and Implementation GC; and Methods GC. In 2000, the Evidence for Policy and Practice Information and Coordinating Centre (EPPI Centre) began supporting review teams in education. EPPI Center develops methods for systematic reviews, supports the training and development of methodological skills for systematic reviewers, and produces systematic reviews across various disciplines and policy sectors. EPPI Center also provides and supports databases containing primary research studies. Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research (AHPSR), hosted by the World Health Organization, supports the generation and synthesis of policy-relevant health systems evidence, tools and methods. AHPSR also provides support for systematic review training, dissemination, and use in order to facilitate evidence-based healthcare. AHPSR established systematic review centers in four low-and middle-income countries (LMICs) in 2007. The same year, the Collaboration for Environmental Evidence (CEE) was registered. CEE seeks to promote and deliver evidence synthesis on issues of environmental management. CEE hosts an open access journal that facilitates the publication of evidence synthesis on issues of environmental management; a library that contains all systematic reviews that have been approved by CEE; and guidelines for planning and conducting environmental management systematic reviews. CEE collaboration has a network of centers around the world. Centers support CEE by promoting evidence based practice and systematic reviews in their region. Currently, there are seven national CEE Centers, based in Canada, France, South Africa, Sweden, and the United Kingdom. The United States of America is host to one international CEE Centre (SEI). More recently, the International Initiative for Impact Evaluation (3ie) was founded in 2008. 3ie produces, synthesizes and promotes evidence on impact evaluation for various developmental projects. Members of the 3ie include NGOs, public and private funders, as well as government agencies from low- and middle-income countries. Together, they make up a diversified global community connected by the common goal of using evidence from rigorous impact evaluations and systematic reviews to improve their policies and programs. The most recent systematic review network is the African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (ACSRM). The ACSRM was established in May, 2022 to promote the production and use of systematic reviews and meta-analyses in low-and middle-income countries. The ACSRM community comprises members from more than 25 countries. The focus of the community has been on systematic reviews related to public health.

posts.title: The Need for The African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (ACSRM)
posts.excerpt: Written by: Fortune B. Effiong In recent times, the use of evidence in making decisions about professional practice and public policy is becoming more common. It started in health care in high-income countries (HICs), and it is gradually expanding to other policy areas and across international borde
posts.text: Written by: Fortune B. Effiong In recent times, the use of evidence in making decisions about professional practice and public policy is becoming more common. It started in health care in high-income countries (HICs), and it is gradually expanding to other policy areas and across international borders. Systematic reviews are scientific approaches to generating systematic and transparent quality-assessed syntheses of research. They are often produced in HICs and are increasingly sought after by clinicians, service consumers, professional bodies, funding agencies, and policymakers to inform decision making. International systematic review networks have developed a variety of strategies to increase researchers' capacity to produce systematic reviews, such as training sessions at conferences; training at reviewing centers; skills-based workshops; accredited face-to-face learning, and online learning. The majority of members in these networks, however, are from high-income countries. Systematic reviews do not adequately benefit Low and Middle Income Countries (LMICs) since they include few LMICs-based authors and studies. Hence, the ability of LMICs to produce reliable evidence for influencing policies is questioned, given the uneven capacity for undertaking this type of research. For instance, from the Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses (SRM)needs assessment survey that we conducted, 78% of LMICs researchers have never conducted a systematic review. The most prominent reason for that was lack of training and skills in SRM (98% of responses). About 36% of them revealed that skill development has been constrained by lack of experienced collaborators and platforms. This means that skills training for individuals will have limited utility if not allied to opportunities for review teams to practice the skills. The training and production of systematic reviews in a country or region, irrespective of income status, is positively correlated with the presence of systematic review networks in that country or region. Hence, the African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses leverages on the framework established by international systematic review organizations and addresses two key gaps left by their interventions: getting more LMICs based scholars and getting more studies from LMICs.

pages.title: Donate
pages.text: Donate to Us Did you know? A large share of public policies and development programmes are implemented without being grounded in rigorous evidence of what works. Across health, education, agriculture, and social protection, this gap between research and decision-making leads to inefficient use of resources and missed opportunities to improve lives. SRN works to change this. We train researchers and policymakers in low- and middle-income countries to generate, understand, and apply systematic reviews and meta-analyses—turning evidence into smarter decisions that improve health systems, strengthen economies, and save lives. pages.title: About Us
pages.text: About US Systematic Reviews Network (SRN), formerly known as the African Community for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (ACSRM), is a registered charity established to support the production, dissemination, and use of systematic reviews and meta-analyses across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). SRN is incorporated as a company limited by guarantee and registered in Nigeria, while operating across Africa and other LMICs through capacity-building programmes, research collaborations, and knowledge-sharing initiatives. SRN was officially launched on 8 December 2022 at the University of Rwanda, Rwanda, and on 19 December 2022 at the University of Lagos, Nigeria, through seed funding received from the International Network for Adavancing Science and Policy (INASP). Our Vision To bridge evidence gaps in LMICs and transform lives by guiding decisions with robust, context-specific evidence. Our Mission To empower researchers from the academia and research institutions especially early career researchers with skills, tools, and resources needed to successfully conduct systematic reviews and meta-analyses. To empower systematic review users (scientists, government agencies, expert panels, patients, policy-makers, health-care advocates) with the knowledge and skills needed to critique, understand, interpret and use systematic reviews and meta-analyses. To cooperate and work with partners, stakeholders, research institutions, and academic institutions to promote and improve the use and production of systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Our Core Values Passsion We have a sense of enthusiasm for our work and for the people around us Teamwork We operate on the principle of teamwork because we believe people are capable of building something bigger than themselves when they unite. Integrity Everyone who represents our team is committed to acting in a way that is consistent with our values. Accountability We accept responsibility for our actions (and inactions) because it is the best way to build trust internally and externally. Quality We uphold the highest standards because we understand that, how well an organization crafts its goods and services determines how successful it is. Diverty and Inclusion We prosper by integrating a variety of backgrounds and experiences into a setting where everyone has an equal opportunity Collaboration We understand the importance of evidence in shaping practice in the global community. Thus, we promote working with different stakeholders towards achieving this aim. Equity We are determined to ensure fairness in all that we do at all times. Our Partners Rising Scholars INASP
